name: Borneo orangutan (Pongo pygmaeus)
description:
The Orangutan of Borneo is a great ape native to the dense tropical forests of Borneo. It is one of the closest living relatives to humans and is known for its intelligence, long reddish-brown hair, and distinctive facial features.
The species was first scientifically described by the Italian naturalist Odoardo Beccari in the 19th century, following his explorations of Borneo’s rainforests. Bornean orangutans are primarily arboreal, spending most of their lives in trees, where they build nests for sleeping and travel through the canopy in search of fruits, leaves, and insects.
Pongo pygmaeus is critically endangered due to habitat loss, deforestation, and hunting. Conservation efforts focus on protecting forests, rescuing and rehabilitating individuals, and educating local communities.


This 3D model was created by Clarissa Bignoli and Erika Del Bene during their Universal Civil Service (SCU) at UniGe.

name: Maiacetus innus  (skeleton cast)
description:
**Object: Model (cast) of *Maiacetus innus* skeleton from exhibition at the  Natural History Museum in Oslo**

Description: *Maiacetus innus*, a ~2.5 m-long Eocene archaeocete, represents an early stage in whale evolution. Its well-developed ankle bones, pelvic-vertebral connection, and shearing molars link it to terrestrial artiodactyl ancestors, while shortened limbs, elongated digits, and conical teeth reflect adaptations for life in water. *Maiacetus* is interpreted as a semiaquatic predator, spending most of its time hunting in aquatic habitats but returning to land to rest and give birth.

Type locality: Kunvit, Pakistan

Geology and Age:Habib Rahi Formation, early Lutetian stage of the middle Eocene,  approximately 47.5 Ma

Photogrametry model created by Maciej Ruciński using RealityCapture

**To read more visit our [blog ](https://norpal.wordpress.com/2024/08/02/maiacetus-a-key-piece-in-the-evolutionary-puzzle-of-whales/)**

description:
3D scan of the skull of a Rüppell's fox (*Vulpes rueppellii*).


Rüppell's fox is a fox species living in desert and semi-desert regions of North Africa, the Middle East, and southwestern Asia. It is a small fox, measuring 66 to 74 cm in total length, including a tail measuring 27–30 cm long with an average weight of 1.7 kg. Rüppell's foxes occupy distinct territories, which they mark with urine, but not with dung as red foxes do. It has an omnivorous diet that varies considerably depending on what is locally available.

Specimen: Rüppell's fox, *Vulpes rueppellii* (Schinz, 1825)

Inventory number: C 1140

name: Tuberculosis Granulomatous in Liver
description:
This interactive 3D model demonstrates a granulomatous lesion within the liver by Tuberculosis , designed for educational purposes in pathology. for Veterinary medicine

The model allows a step-by-step visual exploration of the granuloma structure:

**Outer layer**: Fibrous connective tissue encapsulating the lesion
**Intermediate zone**: Aggregates of inflammatory cells (primarily macrophages and lymphocytes)
**Central core**: Caseation necrosis with areas of calcification, appearing as irregular, pale, cheese-like material

Users can freely navigate, zoom, and explore the internal architecture of the lesion, simulating a progressive microscopic examination from gross structure to cellular detail.

🎯 This model is ideal for:

Medical and pathology students
Visual learners
Interactive teaching and presentations
 
 MADE BY / Doha Essam aly

name: Scipionyx samniticus ("Ciro")
description:
Il modello 3D rappresenta il calco dell'olotipo di Scipionyx samniticus ("Ciro"), primo dinosauro scoperto in Italia (Pietraroja, 113 mln di anni fa). L'originale, lungo 46 cm, è un pulcino di pochi giorni eccezionalmente conservato in 3D: preserva tessuti molli e organi interni unici, tra cui intestino con resti dell'ultimo pasto (pesci e lucertole), fegato, muscoli, trachea e guaine di cheratina. Bipede e predatore, appartiene ai Compsognathidae o a forme giovanili di grandi tetanuri. La presenza del sacco vitellino indica che era appena schiuso, offrendo dati inestimabili su fisiologia, respirazione e sviluppo dei teropodi mesozoici.

⚠️ Nota sulla demo: Scansione dimostrativa eseguita su un calco museale (non sull'originale) in condizioni di luce e ripresa sfavorevoli.

Seppur a bassa risoluzione, il modello è un utile risorsa didattica per scuole e appassionati per esplorare l'anatomia di questo fossile unico al mondo.

name: Sciuridae (ardilla)
description:
La ardilla es un pequeño mamífero conocido por su cuerpo ágil, su larga cola peluda y sus rápidos movimientos. Vive principalmente en los árboles, donde salta de rama en rama gracias a sus fuertes patas y garras afiladas. Su cola grande le sirve para mantener el equilibrio y abrigarse del frío.

Las ardillas se alimentan de nueces, semillas, frutos y, en ocasiones, pequeños insectos. Suelen guardar comida para el invierno, enterrándola en distintos lugares. Son animales muy curiosos y activos, especialmente durante el día. Además, desempeñan un papel importante en los bosques, ya que al enterrar semillas ayudan a que crezcan nuevos árboles.   
Este trabajo va dirigido para enseñar a los estudiantes de 9 grado de Educación General Básica Superior en la materia de Ciencias Naturales. 

El propósito es que los estudiantes sepan las principales características de este animal además de saber de donde proviene, de que se alimentan y cuál es su hábitat.

This is a digital three-dimensional model created in the modeling software ‘blender’ and colored in the ‘Paint3D’ program. Its topology is well optimized for usage on both low-end and high-end devices. Below, I also show the wireframe view of the model to better visualize attachment points and potential placements for bones in ‘blender’s’ Object Mode. This model can be used in a variety of different ways and I have made it accessible to people on SketchFab, Thangs, and Printables. It can be utilized in 3D animation projects or even posed for cinematic shots in software such as ‘blender’, ‘Paint3D’, or ‘Houdini’. It can also be printed using a 3D printer.

Goodbye, the king of the reptile-eaters, Saurophaganax maximus… Welcome Allosaurus anax!

(I made this for fun - I am a beginner in Blender)

3D printing details and settings:
0.2 mm layer height, 0.8 nozzle diameter, PET material, Preferable weight of printed model: 31 g, Printing duration: 3 hours



#Dinosaurs

name: Bovine Skull
description:
High-resolution 3D anatomical scan of a Bovine Skull (Bos taurus).

This digital model provides an accurate representation of the bovine cranial osteology, showcasing the complex structures of the splanchnocranium and neurocranium, including the frontal bones, cornual processes, orbital cavities, and dentition. It serves as a valuable resource for veterinary students, researchers, and digital artists requiring precise biological reference.

Source / Provenance: This specimen is part of the anatomical collection curated by Professor Antonio Palladino, Professor of Veterinary Anatomy, Histology, and Embryology at the University of Rome Tor Vergata (Università degli Studi di Roma Tor Vergata).

Suggested Use: Educational purposes, veterinary research, comparative anatomy study, and scientific visualization.

description:
Yarnaby Wiki:

Yarnaby appears to be a lion-like monster covered in multicolored yarn acting as a sort of mane and fur-like covering all over the body. On his orange-yellow head, two strands of yarn are poking out, giving the yarn the impression of hair. His face consists of two large cartoony eyes with black irises and a big grin with three fangs poking out from his lower jaw. His split-lined face bisects to reveal a large, toothy, fleshy mouth with the two halves connected only by a small hole that leads to the throat and surrounded with more small jagged teeth. Yarnaby walks on all fours with orange-yellow legs with lighter coloured, three-toed paws; his Bigger Bodies form also has sharp bone white claws. Also in the artwork he has no claws.

This is a fan recreation designed by me xerxes3d for the VBunnyGo team for use as a VR avatar.

和名の由来は、半卵形の貝殻を漁師が使う小舟に見立てたものである。殻の上面は黒と淡褐色のまだら模様が現れる。この模様は個体によって色帯や群雲模様になるなど変異がある。岩礁海岸の浅海に生息し、岩陰や転石の下に付着する。

The Japanese name comes from the fact that fishermen liken the semi-oval shell to a small boat. The upper surface of the shell has a mottled pattern of black and light brown. This pattern varies from individual to individual, with some having color bands or cloud-like patterns. It lives in shallow waters along rocky coastlines, attaching itself to rock shadows and under boulders.

name: Ceratosuchus skull cast
description:
From the Science Museum of Minnesota Paleontology Collection. No accession number (yet).
This is a plaster skull cast of a prehistoric crocodilian named Ceratosuchus. 

Due to the cast's uniform color and texture, Dr. Alex Hastings and I ripped up some dinosaur stickers--rip stickers--and put stickers on key areas of the cast so that the 3d modeling software would have an easier time finding landmarks and/or so I could manually allign the model if necessary. 

I kept the stickers in the texture because I think they are fun and they didn't cover anything morphologically significant.

This ancient crocodilian has little horns! I think they are cute.

The shell is thin-walled with low spiral ribs, and finer secondary ribs between the main ribs. A white lubricant layer is present on the inner side of the outer lip of the shell opening. name: Desert Goat (Ammotragus lervia)
description:
This voxel-based Desert/warm Goat is a stylized interpretation of the Barbary Sheep (Ammotragus lervia), a rugged mountain ungulate native to North Africa. With its distinctive curved horns, coarse sandy coat, and solid frame, the model captures the essence of a hardy desert grazer in a simplified, blocky aesthetic. Its compact geometry makes it ideal for educational exhibits, voxel wildlife collections, or game biomes inspired by arid highlands.

 
Taxonomy:

Kingdom: Animalia

Phylum: Chordata

Class: Mammalia

Order: Artiodactyla

Family: Bovidae

Genus: Ammotragus

Species: A. lervia


The Desert/warm Goat (Barbary Sheep) is native to rocky mountains and dry plateaus of North Africa, particularly in regions of Morocco, Algeria, and Chad. It thrives in arid and semi-arid environments, navigating steep cliffs and feeding on sparse grasses and shrubs. Introduced populations also exist in parts of Texas and Spain, where they adapt well to warm, rugged habitats.

name: Dilophosaurus Wetherilli (Jungle skin)
description:

Although the frill and the venom spitting aren't a real part of the animal, it is still an amazing predator, larger than its appearance on-screen. Here, the creature model is reconstructed with our up-to-date understanding of the creature.

The model is a **Production-Ready Rig**, which includes advanced controls for efficient posing and animations, IKs and FKs, bone chains, a Custom UI panel (only available for Blender versions 4.2+), model shape key variations, and custom bone properties.

name: Siamang
description:
3D scan of the skull of siamang (*Symphalangus syndactylus*). 

The siamang is an endangered arboreal, black-furred gibbon native to the forests of Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand. The largest of the gibbons, the siamang can be twice the size of other gibbons, reaching 1 m in height, and weighing up to 14 kg. It inhabits the forest remnants of Sumatra Island and the Malay Peninsula, and is widely distributed from lowland forest to mountain forest—even rainforest—and can be found at altitudes up to 3800 m. The siamang eats mainly various parts of plants.


Specimen: Siamang, *Symphalangus syndactylus* (Raffles, 1821)

Inventory number: C 1594

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa

description:
その美しい色彩と艶が特徴で、貝殻コレクターに人気がある。卵形で周縁は丸く膨らむ。肩の棘は弱い。殻口軸唇は黒褐色で腹面を広く覆う。奄美諸島以南、熱帯西太平洋の水深5～30ｍの砂底。

Characterized by its beautiful colors and luster, it is popular among shell collectors. It is ovoid with a rounded, bulging margin. The shoulder spines are weak. The umbo and labium are dark brown, broadly covering the ventral surface. Found south of the Amami Islands in the tropical western Pacific Ocean at depths of 5 to 30 meters on sandy bottoms.

name: Tortoise
description:
It's a tortoise I made in 3D Coat, as an exercise to learn the software. Usually I use Blender. I really enjoyed 3DCoat, especially the voxel sculpting and the painting. I liked how easy it was to move back and forth from sculpt to paint, and from voxel to surface/multires. I didn't love the retopology tools, mostly because I can already retopologize things in Blender... but I'll definitely use them again for less difficult assets. The UV tools were fast and almost effortless to use.

The tortoise is mostly based on various Galapagos Giant Tortoise pictures I found, but I also took some liberties. The goal was to make it realistic without spending more than 3 days learning the software (Sculpt, paint, retopologize, UV unwrap, bake/export). In the end, I spent the 3 days, thought about it a bit, and used another half day to improve the texture (a lot!) with the knowledge I gained during the first pass. I did the rig/walk-cycle in Blender.

name: Spinosaurus Hybrid
description: In the untamed realms of Isla Sorna, the Spinosaurus emerges as an enigma of the Cretaceous. Towering over its competitors, this colossal predator exhibits a robust sail on its back, shrouded in mystery. With a long, crocodile-like snout and a set of formidable jaws, the Spinosaurus commands the waterways and hunts with unparalleled prowess. name: Castillo de "Manqueospese" o "Aunquespese"
description:
Construido en las décadas de 1470 y 1480 por Pedro Dávila, señor de Villafranca y Las Navas, decidido partidario de los intereses de la infanta Isabel frente al rey Enrique IV y Juana la Beltraneja. 
Se trata de un ejemplo de castillo serrano o montaraz europeo, de muros fuertes adaptados al terreno rocoso en el que se asienta, se le menciona en documentos de los siglos XI y XII como centro de diversas expediciones guerreras y de reconquista contra los musulmanes.
Según la leyenda, el castillo lo mandaría construir don Raimundo, para comunicarse con su amada doña Guiomar, encerrada en el balcón que corona la puerta del Rastro ( en Ávila, acceso por la casa de los Dávila ) , dada la prohibición del padre de ésta de que la pareja continuase con sus amoríos. Ante la actitud paterna, don Raimundo exclamó: "la veré manqueospese " ó  "la veré aunqueospese", y fue entonces cuando levantó su castillo, desde el que al parecer se comunicaba con su querida Guiomar.

description:
O presente projeto estrutural refere-se a uma edificação residencial unifamiliar de dois pavimentos, concebida em estrutura de concreto armado, dimensionada conforme as normas técnicas brasileiras vigentes.

A estrutura foi projetada para garantir segurança, estabilidade, durabilidade e desempenho adequado ao longo de sua vida útil, considerando as ações permanentes e variáveis atuantes, tais como peso próprio, sobrecargas de uso, ações do vento e demais solicitações previstas em norma.

O sistema estrutural é composto por elementos de fundação, pilares, vigas e lajes maciças em concreto armado, devidamente dimensionados e detalhados. As fundações foram definidas de acordo com as características do solo e cargas transmitidas pela superestrutura, podendo ser do tipo sapatas isoladas, blocos ou outro sistema adequado conforme análise geotécnica.

description:
"Gomez and Pugsley are enthusiastic. Morticia is even in disposition, muted, witty, sometimes deadly. Grandma Frump is foolishly good-natured. Wednesday is her mother's daughter. A closely knit family, the real head being Morticia—although each of the others is a definite character— except for Grandma, who is easily led. Many of the troubles they have as a family are due to Grandma’s fumbling, weak character. The house is a wreck, of course, but this is a house-proud family just the same and every trap door is in good repair. Money is no problem."
-Charles Addams[1]
